newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech justice minister and vice-PM resigns - CTK.
newsitem.headline: Czech justice minister and vice-PM resigns - CTK.

text.p: Czech Justice Minister Jan Kalvoda, a deputy premier and leader of a junior partner in the ruling coalition, quit the government and parliament on Tuesday for falsely using an academic title, the CTK news agency said.
Another member of parliament from a coalition party also quit parliament for the same reason, while three other deputies admitted using false titles but did not step down.
Kalvoda was quoted as telling parliament his resignation was connected with a problem over his official academic title, Doctor of Law, but did not elaborate.
According to local media deputies have been questioning the academic titles used by some members of parliament.
CTK said Kalvoda, head of the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), had already informed President Vaclav Havel of his decision to quit because of the improper use of a title he had not attained.
Earlier Pavla Jurkova, a member of another coalition party, the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL), resigned her seat in the 200-seat lower house because of a similar dispute over her law doctorate.

Meanwhile two members of Vaclav Klaus's senior party in the coalition, the Civic Democratic Party (ODS), also admitted on Tuesday that their law doctorates, which were used in campaign material earlier this year, were false, CTK said.
However Anna Roeschova and Ondrej Zemina have not resigned their seats, CTK reported.
A member of the opposition Social Democrats, Marie Noveska, who admitted she had not finished her university course but still used the title doctor of law, has also not resigned, the agency added.
